alignment.note: A word’s way of designating a concept
Dwelling in a sequence of presentations
First element in a derived verb
Uncertain antecedent in the closing line

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Can hardly be called” weakens a categorical denial. Humboldt says that the classification cannot be called purely factual, rather than expressing reluctance or uncertainty about calling it so.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The source denies that the classification is purely factual; it does not attenuate the denial.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Stammwort” is consistently “stem word” here but becomes “base word” in §121:s5. That change obscures the recurrence of the category when Humboldt later distinguishes roots from their role as bases for further formation. “Relative concept” in §74:s5 also leaves less explicit the relational character of being a base.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Stem word now recurs in §121. Clarified that the earlier assertion is relational.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “An imbalance generally rights itself” adopts the contextually persuasive compensatory reading without exposing a difficulty in the supplied wording. Grammatically, the subject of “stellt sich ... her” is the imbalance, which could suggest its establishment or re-establishment rather than its correction. The final clause strongly supports compensation, but the wording warrants an explicit interpretive flag rather than an assumed transcription correction.
decision.resolution: Accepted in part. The result clause supports compensation, so the revised English names the compensating circumstances. The grammatical alternative is preserved in the audit record.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English silently reconstructs the source’s logic and syntax. “We cannot assume an exact knowledge” is not what “sie keine genaue Kenntniss ... voraussetzen” directly says: the German makes the circumstances the apparent subject of “presuppose” and says that they presuppose no exact knowledge. The English supplies a plausible explanation for the difficulty of judging them, but that explanation is an editorial interpretation of a problematic reading.
decision.resolution: Accepted in part. The revision leaves the presupposition impersonal and preserves its negative force. The compressed German remains visible in the decision record.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Compound word sounds” and especially “compound words” can narrow the analysis to lexical compounds. Here the relevant complexity includes the products of the broader formation processes just enumerated: prefixation, suffixation, insertion and other patterned modifications. The translation itself uses the appropriately broader “composite” in §77:s7. A narrow technical reading of “compound” would exclude part of the evidence Humboldt requires for comparison.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Use composite or complex where the source range includes more than lexical compounds alone.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “More directly” selects a reading of “näher” concerning immediacy of derivation. A temporal reading, “more recently”, is also plausible and consequential: the following sentence contrasts these languages with languages transmitted for centuries whose origins disappear into obscurity. The two readings make different claims about why simple forms are absent. The supplied context favours considering the temporal alternative but does not conclusively settle it.
decision.resolution: Retained with the alternative recorded. Näher can convey nearer to the fully formed source in both time and form. The directness reading avoids adding a strictly temporal interval.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Sensations” narrows Empfindungen towards sensory experience in a passage about the inherited life of thought and feeling. The same pairing, Gedanken und Empfindungen, is rendered “thoughts and feelings” in §112:s5, where it likewise describes human experience passing into language. The change here weakens that connection and risks excluding affective experience.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The thought-and-feeling pair belongs to the same topic as the corresponding phrase in §112.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Discerning” renders the practical consequence of geistiger but obscures its explicit reference to the mind. Humboldt is connecting the treatment of sound with intellectual activity, not merely describing more acute auditory discrimination. This matters to the division’s recurring account of sound as shaped by and acting upon the mind.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Adopted intellectually attuned alongside finer.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English explicitly makes the words the bearers of the Gleichartigkeit being investigated. German “ihrer” can refer to either the words or the languages, but the preceding argument expressly concerns “die Gleichartigkeit der Sprachen” (§80:s4) and the inference to historical connection (§80:s6). The English therefore resolves a consequential referential ambiguity in favour of the narrower object of inquiry.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The revision uses the immediately preceding theme of sameness of kind and avoids fixing the possessive to either its grammatical or thematic antecedent alone.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Only occasionally” gives gelegentlich a frequency interpretation. In this contrast between meaning as the basis of composition and sound as a subordinate contributor, “incidentally” or “as occasion arises” is also plausible. The English can consequently make a stronger claim about the infrequency of sound’s involvement than the German requires.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Incidentally better matches the force alongside subordinate.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The historical or genealogical reading of these terms remains obscured. “Mother tongue” normally means a speaker’s native language, whereas Muttersprache here may also mean an ancestral or parent language; the following reference to languages “abhängenden” on German strengthens that possibility. Conversely, “languages that depend on it” can suggest continuing practical or cultural dependence rather than historical derivation. Neither ambiguity should be resolved by silently modernizing Humboldt’s claim about German.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Mother language keeps the shared national language and descent in view. Depend on remains broad since the print names no specific type of historical dependence.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Considered in itself” replaces “as object”, introducing a stronger suggestion of an object independent of its presentation. Later, “the way it is apprehended” can make the presentation itself the thing apprehended, whereas the subjective component concerns the apprehension of the object.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The phrases now distinguish the object qua object and the object being apprehended.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Everything bound to appear on earth” turns dependence on earthly manifestation into an obligation or destiny to appear. The restructuring also obscures the parallel explanatory force of the two indem clauses: both transmission without fettering freedom and the development of languages explain how progress becomes possible.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The two explanatory grounds and the earthly conditions are explicit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Characteriztic” is a repeated misspelling, not an Oxford spelling variant.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Corrected the three occurrences.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English weakens two restrictions supporting the reconciliation of the opposed aspects of the word. “Otherwise opposed qualities” does not convey that the concepts would otherwise cancel one another, and “is a stimulus” omits “nothing but”. The latter matters because Humboldt is denying an independently complete word outside the soul.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Both restrictions hold in the revised wording.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “As the individuality of the speakers, they have attached themselves” is difficult to construe and suppresses the past tense of war. The sentence traces matter and form from the individuality of earlier speakers into sounds and back into living individuality; that movement is not clear in the English.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored the temporal movement into and back out of sound.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: This is an unresolved inconsistency in the checked German, faithfully reproduced in English, rather than an established translation error. §91 says nouns have become adjectives; §93 explicitly describes nouns formed from adjectives. The former also sits awkwardly with its own explanation that names of corporeal objects arise from properties. It should not be silently reversed on contextual grounds.
decision.resolution: Accepted as an annotation. The confirmed print remains in both texts, with the contrary process in §93 and the limit on emending it made explicit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Beyond the particular riches” softens an explicit exclusion into a potentially additive claim. Humboldt says that the partial wealth of images and concepts does not determine linguistic merit; the determining consideration is the general effect on thinking and feeling.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The particular richness is excluded as what determines merit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English accurately reproduces the source’s reference to §90, but the relevant discussion of naming objects through their properties occurs in §91. §90 introduces the distinction between matter and form. Readers following the reference will not find the stated example.
decision.resolution: Retained with the printed reference. The note also directs readers to §91.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English resolves an ambiguity by adding “precisely the same”: it makes the claim concern identical balances across two languages. The German explicitly locates the balance between the different stimuli, allowing a reading about their internal equilibrium. The next sentence, which says one stimulus predominates, supports keeping that alternative visible.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Removed the specification of an identical balance between languages.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “From it emerges the mind’s fortunate capacity for creation” can assert that the distribution of concepts produces the creative capacity. A consequential alternative is evidential: that distribution reveals the creative capacity, continuing the preceding offenbart sich. The German permits this reading, and the paragraph concerns what word formation displays about the mind.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Derives from is plausible alongside geht daraus hervor. The simplified wording keeps emergence without specifying that the distribution itself causes a mental capacity.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The restrictive relative clause in “too many meanings whose ties ... are too loose” makes the prohibition apply specifically to an excessive number of loosely related meanings. The German coordinates excessive number and excessively loose connection, and plausibly presents them as two defects. The English therefore risks narrowing the rule.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The two descriptions are now explicitly coordinated.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Concepts of the mind” and “relations of the mind” can turn geistig into a specification of subject matter: concepts about the mind and relations belonging to it. Here the contrast concerns intellectual or non-sensory concepts and relations more generally, including those expressed through corporeal metaphors.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Intellectual avoids an unintended restriction on the objects of thought.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Motivating meaning” is a defensible but consequential interpretation of Selbstbedeutung that needs an explicit terminological decision. It suggests an explanatory or etymological motivation, whereas the term also stresses the word’s own distinctive manner of designating, as opposed to the object shared with other words. Its antecedent in §98 includes progressively less recoverable designation, ultimately the bare articulated sound.
decision.resolution: Accepted in part. Own and the local guide protect the specifically word-bound meaning while preserving the adopted project term.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Fertilises” and “Symbolising” depart from the stipulated Oxford spelling and from the translation’s own use of “symbolizing” elsewhere.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Corrected both Oxford spellings.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Has the stronger claim to its own rights” shifts an assertion about the natural form maintaining its primacy into language of comparative entitlement. The contrast with §101:s13 is that sound gives way to the concept in a word, while natural form actively maintains its position in a symbol.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Maintaining primacy preserves the active assertion.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: In the quoted passage, “is thus resolved when” replaces an explicit explanation of how the conflict is resolved with a temporal formulation. The infinite’s self-limitation and becoming human are the means of resolution, not merely the occasion.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Rendered the self-limitation and becoming human as the means of resolution.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The added English locator quotes “idea and bodily material coincide”, but the corresponding main-text sentence actually reads “Idea and corporeal material coincide”. The anchor is identifiable, but the apparatus does not quote the frozen translation exactly.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The English locator now reproduces the main-text line exactly.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Different lengths of pause” risks identifying Weile with interruptions between presentations. The contrast developed immediately afterwards is chiefly how long the mind dwells on an individual object: symbolic absorption versus language’s onward movement. This also matters because §102:s7 separately uses Pausen for pauses.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Lingering is distinct from the interruptions mentioned later.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The object of lingering changes. Humboldt says the mind must resist lingering precisely over the obscure and mysterious connection between the sensory and non-sensory. The English instead makes it linger on the connection’s “very obscurity and mystery”, narrowing the target to fascination with those qualities.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The object of lingering is the connection itself.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “What accompanies the same word ... differs” avoids resolving the German ellipsis but also removes its explanatory content. The immediate context most naturally supplies different sensory presentations, explaining the preceding claim about their character. Different states of mind remain a possible antecedent from the earlier sentences.
decision.resolution: Retained with the alternative recorded. The preceding grammatical candidate is also the dispositions that affect presentation. Supplying presentations gives a narrower argument than the German obliges.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “In those dialects” fixes da exclusively to the popular dialects of the preceding sentence. The reference can encompass the broader discussion of languages of uncultivated peoples, which is resumed by the contrast with highly cultivated nations in §105:s9. The English therefore makes a consequential narrowing that the German does not require.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Here leaves the scope of the reference open.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘At no moment of its life complete’ can blur the distinction between being a whole at every moment (§§107–108) and having finished developing. The context partly protects the English, but ‘abgeschlossen’ concerns finality here, not the absence of present wholeness.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Finished preserves the distinction between development still in progress and a whole at any given moment.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘Mode of viewing’ and ‘mode of sensory viewing’ obscure the recurrence of Anschauungsweise, rendered ‘mode of intuition’ in §§91 and 93. This matters particularly in §120, where Anschauungsweise and Auffassung occur together and should remain recognizably distinct.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Mode of intuition recurs where it names Anschauungsweise. Apprehension remains distinct in §120.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English makes the ‘spirit of a language’ the recipient of the resonance. A contextually stronger parsing takes ‘dem Geiste’ as the human mind receiving it and ‘einer Sprache’ as a preposed genitive belonging to ‘Gehalt’: a language’s content of human existence resounds to the mind. This connects directly with the preceding accumulation of thoughts and feelings in language and the resulting stimulating power. The printed syntax permits competing attachments, so this requires adjudication rather than silent textual correction.
decision.resolution: Retained with a reading note. The immediate attachment of einer Sprache to Geiste is the unmarked parsing. The possibility of a genitive with Gehalt is supported by the argument and has a consequentially different recipient.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘Concepts of the mind’ can suggest concepts whose subject matter is the mind. Here geistige Begriffe contrasts broadly with the particular objects just mentioned and continues the discussion of non-sensory concepts; its scope is not explicitly confined to psychological concepts.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Intellectual concepts is broader than concepts whose objects are mental entities.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘Characteriztic’ is a typographical error, not an Oxford spelling.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Corrected the spelling to characteristic.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘It is therefore by no means necessary’ presents non-necessity as the conclusion of §120. The German more naturally blocks a possible inference from that section: the existence of general designating concepts does not thereby require a stock of root words from which all other words originate. The following discussion explicitly separates semantic designation from exhaustive derivation.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Blocked the inference from a system of semantic relations to exhaustive derivation from roots.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘Base words’ changes the established rendering of Stammwörter as ‘stem words’ in §§74 and 76. Here the relation between Wurzelwörter and Stammwörter is itself under discussion, so an unexplained new English term can suggest a third category.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Stem words is consistent with the earlier sections. The guide was updated to use that wording.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘Names derived from those of peoples’ gives Gentilitia a specific derivational source that the German label does not state. It can exclude formations indicating geographical origin and makes the example turn on derivation from an existing people-name rather than on the category designated.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Gentilic names retains the historical classification without implying a particular derivation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: ‘Here I can give only’ reads as a limitation on the examples available or permitted. The German construction more naturally means that merely mentioning these examples suffices, as the ensuing explanation confirms.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The wording now indicates that the examples suffice for the purpose.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Seele becomes ‘mind’ here, although the division generally renders it ‘soul’ and reserves ‘mind’ for Geist. This passage explicitly resumes the earlier account of the word’s effects, so the changed term conceals that continuity.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored soul and the link to the account resumed from §105.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English silently resolves a meaningful pronominal difficulty by supplying ‘these changes’ as what linguistic study must include. That is contextually persuasive, but the checked German has masculine singular ‘ihn’, not a pronoun agreeing with the changes or their study. Its nearest masculine antecedent is the ‘material … part of language’, which would yield a different and contextually awkward claim. The supplied material does not establish a correction.
decision.resolution: Accepted as an annotation. The English continues the study of the changes. The note records the pronoun, the nearest grammatically compatible antecedent and the grounds for the contextual choice.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Added qualification weakens a categorical distinction. English 'cease to be language in their own right' softens German 'ist nicht mehr Sprache, sondern nur Element derselben', which denies syllable and letter the status of language without the limiting phrase 'in their own right'.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Reintroduced the categorical distinction between language and its elements.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Bearer of 'eignen' is obscured. 'An ideal world of its own' can be read as the word's own world, whereas the definite German phrase, in a clause about language as a whole replacing the actual world (cross-referenced to §39), points to the particular ideal world belonging to language. The indefinite 'an' also loses the definiteness of 'der eignen ideellen Welt'.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Assigned the ideal world to language as a whole in the English, following §39.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Quantifier scope is settled in one of two plausible ways. English 'a large proportion of languages' counts languages. German 'ein grosser Theil aller ... Sprachen' can also be read as a large part of every such language (i.e. of its vocabulary) being reducible to monosyllabic roots, which better supports the claim in p74:s2 that the monosyllabic division is not purely factual. The German is genuinely ambiguous and should not be silently resolved.
decision.resolution: Retained. Aller Sprachen supplies the population of languages from which ein grosser Theil selects. The proposed distribution to every language’s vocabulary would require a different quantifier scope and lacks support in the next clause.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Uncertain rendering of the compensation mechanism. English 'an imbalance generally rights itself' makes the imbalance its own agent of correction. German 'stellt sich ein Misverhältniss ... durch andre ... Umstände her' is idiomatically obscure with Misverhältniss as subject; the sense required by the result clause is that the disproportion is made good or compensated for by other circumstances, not that it re-establishes itself. The present wording obscures whose state is restored.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The English now names the accompanying circumstances as what compensates for the imbalance. The result clause supports the contextual interpretation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Subject and presupposition are reversed in interpretation. English 'because we cannot assume an exact knowledge of how discourse is actually delivered' supplies 'we' and a lack of knowledge. German literally says the circumstances are harder to judge 'als sie keine genaue Kenntniss ... voraussetzen' — inasmuch as they presuppose no exact knowledge of living delivery. Whether Humboldt means that judgement must proceed without such knowledge, or that no such knowledge is available to presuppose, is not settled by the syntax; the English chooses the second without signalling the difficulty.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Keep the lack of presupposed knowledge without supplying an unambiguous agent. The German itself gives no independent cause beyond its compressed clause.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Wrong bearer for 'dieselben'. English 'the organs of speech and their laws are everywhere the same, making the same limited range of word sounds possible' transfers sameness to organs and laws. In German the subject is 'die Gleichheit der Sprachwerkzeuge und ihrer Gesetze', and 'dieselben ... Wortlaute' is its object: the sameness of organs and laws makes the same word-sounds, and only a certain number of them, possible everywhere.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. The earlier two clauses expressed both samenesses. Recast them to make the argument and its subjects explicit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Narrowed recasting. German asks sound-identity/affinity to decide 'über ihren historischen oder physiologischen Unterschied' — over the historical or physiological distinction/difference in question. English 'whether the resemblance is historical or physiological in origin' adds 'in origin' and turns a distinction to be decided into a classification of a resemblance, easing but also narrowing the §47 problem cross-referenced here.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored the distinction referred to in §47 without treating origin as the only conceivable interpretation of Unterschied.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Modality strengthened. German 'dürften höchstens ... auszunehmen seyn' is tentative and maximal: at most, imitative words might be excepted. English 'The only possible exceptions ... are words that imitate natural sounds' asserts that such exceptions exist and are the only ones.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored the tentative upper bound for possible exceptions.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Humboldt's sound-formation terms are paraphrased into generic additions, collapsing distinctions. 'Anklang' becomes 'echo', 'Anhängung, Vorschlag oder Einschiebung' becomes addition 'at the end, at the beginning, or within it', and 'Erweiterungen ... durch Vor- und Nachklänge' becomes extension 'by sounds added at the beginning or end'. The Klang metaphor and the difference between derivation by accretion and resonance-like recurrence are no longer terminologically visible, though §§77–78 turn on classifying just these processes.
decision.resolution: Retained. The three physical locations and the separate operation of echoing preserve the contrasts. Sound additions at the front or back convey Vor- und Nachklänge without ascribing a modern morphological category.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Two directional choices settle ambiguous German. (a) 'Je näher eine Sprache aus einer schon vollständig geformten entnommen ist' is rendered 'the more directly derived', choosing directness of derivation over closeness (temporal or genealogical proximity) of the taking. (b) 'steigt sie zu einfachen Lauten auf' (ascends to simple sounds in analysis) becomes 'reaches back to', temporalising an analytic ascent. Both affect the §79 contrast with languages whose origin is lost in obscurity.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Leads back up keeps the analytic ascent in a historical inquiry. Directness is plausible and the English should leave its precise genealogical or temporal measure open.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Referent and force of 'in sich' are settled. 'Acts in its own right' imports independent standing; German 'auch in sich ... auf die Nation zurück[wirkt]' more plainly contrasts an effect in itself (in consciousness and feeling), beyond its effect on use. In the next clause the pronoun in 'womit sie in Berührung steht' (Nation or Spracherzeugung, both feminine) is rendered by an ambiguous English 'it' after 'production of language among its people', leaving the bearer of fruitfulness unclear.
decision.resolution: Retained with the alternative recorded. The juxtaposition of use and the direct effect on the nation already conveys the contrast. Both nation and linguistic production remain possible for the following pronoun.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Recurring term mistranslated. 'Geistiger' is rendered 'discerning' ('more refined and discerning the ear and the sense of language'). Elsewhere in the division geistig is kept as intellectual/mental, and the contrast feiner und geistiger is central to Humboldt's claim that fineness of hearing is also intellectuality of language-sense. 'Discerning' reduces this to perceptual acuity.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Intellectual attunement is distinct from fineness and preserves the force of Geist.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Inconsistent and potentially misleading rendering of the technical Gleichartigkeit / gleichartig (see §47 in the background). Within a few pages it is 'similarity in kind' (p80:s4, p80:s6), 'in what respects ... are of the same kind' (p81:s1), 'to be of the same kind' (p81:s5, note). 'Similarity' suggests mere resemblance, whereas Humboldt's argument in §§80–81 distinguishes historically grounded sameness of kind, knowable through lexical analogy, from merely apparent sound-resemblance (p81:s5). The variation obscures that one concept is at issue.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Regularized the nominal form as sameness of kind and the related adjective as of the same kind. The argument itself distinguishes this from a mere similarity in sound.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Strength and noun changed at the clause end. German: a language 'in welcher gar kein solcher Bau in solcher Vollkommenheit, oder ein andres System desselben vorhanden ist' — in which no such structure in such completeness/perfection at all, or another system of it, is present. English 'absent in that degree of development, or follows a different system' loses 'gar kein', replaces Vollkommenheit (completeness/perfection) with developmental degree, and shifts the subject of the alternative from a system being present to the structure following a system.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored the alternative structures and the completeness qualification in the receiving language.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: A syntactically odd printed reading is silently smoothed. German 'wie es in hloili auch loili ist' does not literally say 'just as hloili also occurs as loili'; the English supplies 'occurs as'. That is a plausible sense, but because the clause carries the evidential parallel for treating h as mere aspiration, the smoothing should be recorded rather than presented as transparent. No alternative reading is asserted here.
decision.resolution: Retained with the uncertainty recorded. Occurs as conveys the relation needed in the comparison without asserting a direction of derivation the text does not give.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Epistemic uncertainty added to Humboldt's example. German has a wenn–so construction: if/when the emergence of λαμβάνω from λάβω 'blosse Tonveränderung ist'. English 'may be a mere change of sound' introduces a tentative 'may' absent from the conditional assertion, presenting Humboldt's historical claim as hedged. Preserve his claim as his, without modernising caution.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Kept the German conditional comparison without imposing a new hedge.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Modernising narrowing. 'Bildung durch Vor- und Nachsilben' (fore- and after-syllables) is rendered 'formation by prefixes and suffixes'. Prefix/suffix in current English need not be syllabic and belongs to a later morphological taxonomy; Humboldt's compound-by-syllables framing in §82, where Lautverhältnisse are said to cooperate only subordinately, is thereby tidied.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Rendered the cited syllables descriptively, preserving what Humboldt counts as the formative material.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Cross-cutting collapse of Ton and Laut (and Klang) into indiscriminate 'sound'. The preceding Lautsystem division (§§56–71, background) and §§73–83 themselves exploit the difference between Laut as articulated sound (Wortlaut, Lautsystem, Wahl der Laute, Lautverhältnisse) and Ton as tone/sounded tone (Tonbehandlung, Tonveränderung, Grundton, Verhältnis zwischen Ton und Bedeutung). Rendering both as 'sound' throughout — e.g. 'treatment of sound' for Tonbehandlung in p82:s1 immediately before 'sound relationships' for Lautverhältnisse in p82:s4 — makes it impossible for the English reader to see when Humboldt shifts level, notably in §83's move from choice of Laute to Ton–meaning agreement.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Restored tone for Grundton and the specifically treated alteration in §80. Many local Ton and Laut uses overlap in this print. The guide records the distinction where the opposition matters and avoids a blanket pitch interpretation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “als Object” is rendered “considered in itself”, importing the distinct “an sich” contrast of §85:s2 and obscuring that the object qua object is at issue.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The point concerns the object qua object, and the rendering now differs from the earlier in itself.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The technical verb “vergeistigt” is rendered inconsistently and freely, first as “gives mental form to” and later as “draws … towards the life of the mind”. The first imports “form”; the second changes a direct transformation of the human being into movement towards a state.
decision.resolution: Retained with a conditional term choice. A common spiritualizes misleadingly suggests a religious or metaphysical process here. In §89 the verbs generalizing and taking bodily form identify the mental transformation. In §105 the ascent to intellectuality guides the English.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The exclusion in “nichts als eine Anregung” is dropped, weakening the contrast between the word outside the soul as nothing but a stimulus and the completed concept in the soul as thinking itself.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The restriction is restored and remains distinct from actual thinking.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The bearer “eine … Individualitaet”, a technical term throughout §§86–92, is recast twice as a “person”. This obscures the level at which Humboldt is arguing — individuality within, and against, the generality of language.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Very different individuality remains the explicit condition on apprehension and the language’s form is the active force. English idiom supports a person as the bearer of individuality.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Unresolved textual/semantic reversal: the checked German of §91:s8, faithfully followed in English as “nouns that have become adjectives”, says substantives have become adjectives, although the properties-premise in the same sentence and §93:s4 (“Substantiva … aus Adjectiven bildend”) require the opposite direction. The uncorrected whole-work OCR shows the same order, so this cannot be settled from the supplied material as a transcription error; the editor must decide between retaining a printed/manuscript reading with a note and an emendation.
decision.resolution: Retained from the print; annotated. The phrase on p. 421 is confirmed from the scan. The source and translation preserve the order and the reader note makes the contrary §93 account visible. Manuscript collation remains outstanding.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The German “nicht durch … sondern durch” contrast is lost in “… effect …, beyond the particular riches …”, which can be read as adding the riches rather than excluding them as the criterion of linguistic merit.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The revised pair of sentences preserves the exclusion of a partial stock as criterion.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The parenthetical qualification “ohne anderer geringerer zu erwähnen” (“without mentioning other, lesser [disadvantages]”) is omitted; “among its disadvantages” only partly compensates.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The mention of lesser disadvantages is restored.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Cross-reference: the designation of objects by their properties was introduced at §91:s8, not §90:s1 (objective/subjective, matter/form). English reproduces “§90” without comment.
decision.resolution: Retained with the print reference and a reader note linking §91. The print does not specify a different marginal number.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Ambiguous referent of “Gleichgewicht” resolved, without warrant, as two languages having the “same balance” as each other. §94:s2, on one stimulus predominating over another, supports the alternative that equilibrium within a language’s word-form is itself rarely perfect.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The revised wording keeps two languages and a perfect balance, leaving the emphasis on the word-form balance and its variation.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The antecedent of “durch diesen” is left undecidable by “which in turn helps determine it”: German “diesen” most nearly refers to the character of the literature (not to “use” or “literature” itself), and “helps” has no German counterpart there.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Both directions of influence are now explicit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “mit welchen wir hier zunächst zu thun haben” is rendered “with which we are primarily concerned”, losing the deictic “here in the first instance” that points back to the American languages framing the whole work (cf. §75:s6).
decision.resolution: Accepted. Keep the immediate, text-internal restriction on the languages under consideration.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “eine Masse Gedankenstoffes” becomes merely “a body of material”: the recurring term Gedankenstoff (“material of thought”, §72:s5, §96:s3) is dropped at the point where the benefit is made conditional on its bearing on thinking.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The condition expressly involves a body of material of thought.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “glückliche” in Humboldt’s evaluative sense of a happy/felicitous endowment is rendered “fortunate” of the creative capacity (suggesting luck) and “natural” of the disposition to symbolize, losing the recurrent term and its positive valuation.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Both expressions now retain the positive sense of a gift. Felicitous would sound like an evaluation of the wording rather than of the endowment.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The pivotal claim that what indicates the concept is itself, “auch als Begriff”, its designation is paraphrased into “is what designates it, and this too is a concept”, which blurs the identity being asserted and prepares §99:s1 poorly. “in dem ganzen Wesen” also becomes merely “in its entirety”, losing “essence/nature”.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The substance of the object and the conceptual status of its designation are explicit.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Anschauungsweise” is rendered elsewhere in the block as “mode of intuition” (§§91–93), but here as “manner of sensory apprehension” / “sensory mode of apprehending”. “Sensory” is already inserted in §98:s6, although §98:s7 then argues that this mode can only be conceived as sensory; the sequence of the argument is obscured.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The sensory restriction is inferred in the next block; Anschauungsweise and Auffassungsweise remain distinct there.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Humboldt’s coinage “Selbstbedeutung” is uniformly rendered “motivating meaning”. This imports the later linguistic notion of (etymological) motivation and erases the “self-/its own” element by which the word signifies through the concept grasped in it; it is a defensible interpretation but not a neutral equivalent, and it governs §§99–104.
decision.resolution: Retained with clarification. Own restores Selbst at the introduction; the guide explains that the term covers the conceptual designation and distinguishes a historical reconstruction from what speakers still feel.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “wohl mit Recht … ansehen muss” is weakened to “presumably have good reason”, and “das Ursprünglichere” (the more original state) is narrowed to “an earlier state in the history of languages”, adding “history”.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The revision retains the comparative original condition and the force of the qualified must.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “es schiebt der Idee eine Gestalt unter” becomes the neutral “it supplies the idea with a shape”. “Unterschieben” carries slipping/substituting something under or in place of the idea, which matters to the ensuing distinction between word and symbol.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The image of setting a shape in place of the idea better preserves unterschieben.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Weile” (length of tarrying/dwelling) in §102:s4 is rendered “lengths of pause”, collapsing it into the distinct “Pausen” term used in §102:s7 and misdescribing the symbolizing mind’s lingering on an object as a gap between presentations.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Lingering in the succession and the light interruptions of it are distinct. The 1906 text reads Weile.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Checked German prints the noun as “Gäbe”, orthographically anomalous for “Gabe” (gift) and formally indistinguishable from a subjunctive form; English silently normalizes to “gift”. This is a meaningful ambiguity for the German apparatus, not a translation error in sense.
decision.resolution: Retained in English and recorded. Enlarged p. 430 shows Gäbe; the noun Gabe is required by context, coordinated with Drang. The German remains as printed.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The German is elliptical: “von verschiedenen … begleitet” has no head noun (evidently the sensory presentations of §104:s11). English masks the ellipsis by recasting to “What accompanies the same word … plainly differs…”, leaving the reader unable to see what Humboldt left unexpressed. “Vortrage” as “exposition” also narrows delivery/discourse to expository writing.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Use discourse for Vortrag. The German can take the ellipsis up from the preceding dispositions as well as from presentations, so the English leaves its referent open.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “Gemüth(-)” is rendered three ways within §105: “inner life” (§105:s1 “Empfindung des Gemüths”), “affective” (§105:s1 “Gemüthskräfte”), and “of the heart” (§105:s5 “Gemüthsempfindung”). The recurrence of a central anthropological term is lost and its scope shifts from affect to heart to inner life.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Inner life now recurs for Gemüth and Gemüthsempfindung. Affective powers makes the functional contrast within the compound clear; the guide connects them.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The contrast “Volksdialecte” / “höhere gereinigte Mundart” is weakened by rendering Mundart as “idiom” and “gereinigte” as “refined”, losing both the dialect-vs.-dialect parallelism and the notion of purification of the higher form.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. Dialect is restored. Refined aptly expresses gereinigt in the argument about cultivation; purified risks suggesting exclusion of foreign admixture.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: “in der fesselfreien Rede” is explicated as “discourse free of metrical constraints”. The prose reference in §105:s10 makes this plausible, but the metaphor of fetters and the generality of “unfettered discourse” are prematurely narrowed to metre.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored the metaphor and left specification of prose to the next sentence.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: House-spelling/typography: “characteriztic” occurs three times in the block (for characteristic); “Symbolising” (§102:s5) breaks the block’s otherwise Oxford -ize- practice (“symbolizes”, “symbolizing”, “synthesizing”, “individualizing”).
decision.resolution: Accepted. Corrected the three typographical errors and initial Symbolizing.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: German Erfahrung is rendered as historical evidence, shifting the ground from historical experience to documentary evidence.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Erfahrung remains experience.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The recurring key term Anschauungsweise, rendered as mode of intuition in §§91-94, becomes mode of viewing and mode of sensory viewing here. Viewing narrows Anschauung to the visual and breaks the terminological chain; at p110 the mode one works towards also becomes one the speaker seeks to bring about.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Mode of intuition recurs and the intended orientation in §110 is unchanged.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Genauer bestimmen is rendered as giving more precise definition. Definition narrows bestimmen and sits awkwardly with the point that the finer determination in use need not be demonstrable in a dictionary.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Determination can occur through use without a formulated definition.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Gebrauch becomes choice, and sprachkundigen Rednern, speakers who know the language, becomes speakers with a practised sense of language. Knowledge of the language and its origins, which explains why freedom and liberty differ in use despite differing only in origin, is replaced by practised taste.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The English again concerns use by linguistically knowledgeable and sensitive speakers.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Erschöpfenden Ausdruck, exhaustive expression, is weakened to fully adequate expression, lowering the criterion for words to be collected as lacking equivalents elsewhere.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored the force of exhaustive.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Kraft, elsewhere the active power at work in language, is rendered as capacity, a merely potential ability, where the amount of the world actually transformed into language is at issue.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Power and opportunity are distinct conditions.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English reads 'characteriztic operations', a misspelling of characteristic. The same misspelling recurs outside this block at p87:s1, p89:s3 and p97:s5.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Corrected characteristic throughout.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Schweben, consistently rendered as hover elsewhere in the division, for example the word hovering in the sphere of imagination at §89, is rationalised as stand highest, losing Humboldt's suspended-motion metaphor for the most general words.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Retained the image of hovering above the other words.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The English lists four labels, nouns, adjectives and adverbs, or verbs, and then speaks of one of these three classes. The German has three Gattungen corresponding to §118's objects, qualities and actions, with adjectives and adverbs forming the single quality class, but the English punctuation makes the count self-contradictory. Grammar can also weakens the German's categorical statement that grammar recasts them.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The central class is explicitly the one that includes adjectives and adverbs.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Uncertainty in the German is silently resolved. Eines ursprünglichen has no expressed noun, but the English supplies an original verb as the first member combined with an original stem. The English also turns the awkward so wesentlich ... dass construction into a causal for. The verb reading is plausible for incorporated stems, but an original word or stem cannot be ruled out from the wording alone.
decision.resolution: Partly accepted. The revision avoids the stronger causal reading, and a note preserves the choice of verb from the nearest expressed class and the equally possible stem from the parallel phrase.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Nicht gleich durchgehend means not equally thoroughgoing or universal; applies less consistently recasts the difference as irregularity of application rather than extent.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The degree of application is distinct from consistency.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Stammwörter is rendered as base words, although Stammwort is consistently stem word at §§74-76 and Stamm is stem at p118:s9. The change obscures the claim that root words serve as stem words for derivation and compounding and blurs the root/stem distinction on which §§121 and 123 depend.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Retained the root/stem relation with stem word in both places.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The Latin technical term Gentilitia is replaced by the explanatory gloss names derived from those of peoples. That narrows a traditional class of denomination by people, country or descent to derivations from peoples' names and may misstate its basis.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Gentilic names avoids adding a specific derivational source.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Verbindung der Rede and Zusammenfügung der Rede are both narrowed to joining words. That obscures the technical discourse-connexion that is the subject of the next division, Redeverbindung from §127, and the distinction between forming the vocabulary and connecting discourse.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Connection and construction of discourse now link to the following division.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Logische Zweckmässigkeit is rendered as logical propriety. Zweckmässigkeit is fitness for a purpose, not propriety or correctness, and Humboldt's criterion is teleological: rule-governed formation is fit only where the classes derive purely from concepts.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The proposed restriction is what better serves a logical purpose.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Sphäre is rendered as entire domain, although Sphäre is kept as sphere elsewhere, for example at p86, p89 and p125. Domain imports Gebiet language and entire strengthens filling a sphere into exhausting a whole field.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Kept the sphere metaphor and the stated extent.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The spatially conflated pairs are made hard to read. Humboldt names two different concepts that several languages unite under one expression, using German labels for the concepts. As in schmal narrow and eng tight, or breit broad and gross large can be read as citing two separate German expressions, the opposite of the conflation being described.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Expressed the pairs as concept labels and preserved the German forms separately.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Seele is rendered as mind, although Seele is consistently soul and Geist is mind or spirit throughout §§85-105. This collapses the soul/mind distinction at the point where the argument turns to the words' effect back upon the soul.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored Seele as soul.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The explicit resultative link daraus entstehen is omitted. The English merely adds a simultaneous consequence, weakening Humboldt's claim that the intellectual disposition itself produces the more superficial mode of designation.
decision.resolution: Accepted. The disposition is the cause of the result described.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: Sich unterschieben, a different sense slipping in underneath the same expression, becomes simply acquiring different senses. Acquisition suggests added senses rather than substitution under an unchanged sound, which is the mechanism distinguished in §126 from overt meaning change at §84.
decision.resolution: Accepted. Restored the image of a different sense coming in under the expression.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; English and annotation review pending
decision.question: The pronoun ihn is left without a grammatically concordant antecedent. Ihr Studium is neuter, the changes are plural, and the nearest masculine nouns are Kreis and Theil, neither of which fits as what linguistics must include. The English resolves the object as these changes, where the sense may rather be their study or this whole subjective domain. The checked German and the uncorrected background agree on ihn, so this is a genuine referent ambiguity, not a settled reading.
decision.resolution: Accepted as an annotation. The English contextual supplement remains provisional and the printed form and its nearest antecedent are identified in the reader note.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Accent joins sounds
decision.resolution: The local noun is implicit. §68 explains how accent brings several articulated sounds together into the unity of a word.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Historical and physiological explanation
decision.resolution: §47 explains why similarity of sound cannot decide the distinction. Keep its wording broad enough to leave open the precise historical process.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Object and presentation
decision.resolution: Presentation names what becomes present in thought, distinct from the object as object. The object is what a person apprehends.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: A language-specific view
decision.resolution: The view comes from the ways a language makes concepts available. §86 preserves differences among individuals who share a language.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Matter and form of the word
decision.resolution: This label belongs to the threefold way of bringing objects before the soul. The contrasting form concerns cooperation of faculties. Form denotes the cooperation of faculties in the same three respects. The definition is local to the word.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Direction of derivation
decision.resolution: The order is confirmed on p. 421. The converse in §93 makes a reversal plausible. Preserve the print and signal the difference at both anchors in the records.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: A word’s way of designating a concept
decision.resolution: This is the word-specific designation through a selected conceptual aspect. §99 asks separately whether speakers still feel the motivation and whether an investigator can recover it.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Dwelling in a sequence of presentations
decision.resolution: The print reads Weile. §102:s5 and the deleted passage under §101 contrast dwelling with movement. §102:s7 separately concerns breaks and pauses.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: The bearer of the resonance
decision.resolution: Keep the straightforward attachment of the genitive to Geist. A preposed genitive with Gehalt gives another plausible reading, in which the substance held in the language resounds to a human mind.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: First element in a derived verb
decision.resolution: Verba supplies the closest stated class. The parallel with the original stem also permits original stem as the first constituent.

decision.authority: Coordinator under D040; provisional source-based interpretation
decision.question: Historical classifier for possession
decision.resolution: The label is glossed through the factual relation of possession mentioned later. No example in §122 establishes its grammatical realization.

decision.question: Reader note: coptic-sanskrit
decision.resolution: One might take Coptic *hrosch* and Sanskrit *rôsha*, both meaning ‘anger’, to be of the same kind. The *h* might be a mere aspiration of the *r*, just as *hloili* also occurs as *loili*. Closer comparison, however, shows that *hrosch* arose from *horsch*, which has the same meaning, just as *hroyr* arose from *hoyrooy* and *heri*. The resemblance in sound to the Indian word is therefore merely accidental. (Humboldt)

The example of naming for a property occurs in §91. §93 refers in print to §90. The manuscript reading remains to be checked. (Trans.)

decision.question: Reader guide: concept-object-presentation
decision.resolution: A *presentation* is how an object becomes present to someone’s mind. The object can be corporeal or formed by the mind. A word gives the concept a shape from a particular standpoint, and the presentation given by the word continues to act alongside the individual’s presentation of the object. *Apprehension* names the way of taking up the object.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: word-sound
decision.resolution: The sound of a word can continue across generations while its content varies. The German terms for sound overlap. In §91 *Schall* draws attention to the audible sound that may stay the same even when the word as actually thought or spoken changes.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: form-and-matter
decision.resolution: In §90 a word’s *matter* is how it presents objects along the logical, sensory and affective lines set out in §87. Its *form* is how the faculties work together in those respects. In §89 sensory and affective content is transformed by imagination, which can preserve it as form. *Material* also names what the words provide for discourse in §72.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: motivating-meaning
decision.resolution: The *motivating meaning* is what gives a word its particular way of designating a concept. It can lie in a perceptible feature of a thing or in a metaphor. Humboldt distinguishes cases where speakers still feel the motivation from those where a historical investigator can recover it.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: word-sign-symbol
decision.resolution: A sign in the strict sense designates something with an existence of its own. A concept takes its completed shape through a word. The natural form of a symbol can stand on its own, and its idea can be seen throughout that form. A word can have symbolic properties even though its sound and concept have the more tightly joined relation described in §101.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: view-of-the-world
decision.resolution: Each language makes a view of the world available through its ways of forming and designating concepts. There is room within that view for individual modes of presentation and for changes in language and thought over time.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: stem-word-root
decision.resolution: A stem word is a starting point for an analysis of word formation. Root words can serve as stem words for derivation and composition and are constrained in connected discourse. The analysis traces relative starting points. Humboldt also rejects the forced assignment of every word to a proposed root.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: feeling
decision.resolution: The term *feeling* includes the intellectual orientation that operates without clear reflective awareness in forming and using words. §105 distinguishes particular emotions from a combined intellectual and affective disposition. *Inner life* renders *Gemüth* where its affective capacities matter.

decision.authority: Coordinator applying approved D029 and D039 policies under D040; review pending
decision.question: Reader guide: words-of-possession
decision.resolution: Humboldt lists *words of possession* among families formed by a recurring procedure. He explains the basis of the class through a factual relation of possession. The passage gives no forms from which to identify a particular grammatical category.

The English largely preserves this progression, including Humboldt’s historical claims and the distinction between historical evidence and psychological influence in §83. The heading and all three notes have no consequential content mismatch. The principal concerns are unmarked interpretation of difficult printed wording in §§74–75, the scope and purpose of lexical comparison, and several consequential terminology choices. Across the division, §§98 and 123 confirm the scope of §§73–82, §93 resumes §83’s sound–meaning argument, and §121 makes consistent treatment of Stammwort particularly useful. The later emphasis on use and subjective response also develops §72’s warning against judging a language from isolated vocabulary."}, {"block": 2, "assessment": "The block moves from the relative persistence of sounds and variability of meanings to the word’s object, individual presentation, matter and form; it then examines conceptual boundaries, designation, symbols and accompanying feeling. The English broadly preserves that architecture, the historical claims and the distinction between authorial notes and editorial deletions; p104:s5–s6 remains coherent across the ID boundary. The principal concerns are local changes in logical force, referents and interpretive scope. Several findings identify plausible alternatives rather than established errors. The noun/adjective reversal and §93’s reference to §90 are problems already present in the supplied German and require transparent editorial handling. Terminological decisions about Selbstbedeutung and geistig should remain compatible with §§113–120, while the treatment of feeling anticipates §§124–126. No critical reversal of the block’s overall argument was found."}, {"block": 3, "assessment": "All 130 requested IDs were compared, including the editorial Havestadt note and the sentence spanning p122:s4–s5. The block moves from individual words to the vocabulary as an interconnected whole: its capacity for development, kinds of richness, comparative assessment, classificatory and derivational resources, and finally its subjective effects and historical transformation. The English largely preserves this structure, the methodological qualifications in §§113–114, and Humboldt’s historical claims. The principal decisions concern the recipient of resonance in §112, the inference blocked in §121, the scope of Gentilitia, and the unresolved pronoun in §126. Cross-block terminology should preserve the distinctions among Anschauungsweise, Auffassung, Seele, Geist, Stammwort and Wurzelwort. The closing account of subjective change returns to §§72, 84–94 and 105 and prepares the transition to discourse combination."}], "inputs": ["eba466b3fadf211397d99a86d44ac167bb87d3b6916cc93b0d0ab1edc9ba6c09", "01d1422643d65941bbc54efc1ef4ff49fbac8021bbb0ac2086d6c19cdd75816a", "ea8bd0834210bc6b97c5d0314c02e71f1dc634adcaa5f79dad2ab8e72a142751"]}

evidence.excerpt: It is striking that Chinese, despite its paucity of spoken words, does not run each possible word through all the available tones. Still less does it combine all final vowels with every initial consonant.

evidence.excerpt: One might take Coptic *hrosch* and Sanskrit *rôsha*, both meaning ‘anger’, to be of the same kind. The *h* might be a mere aspiration of the *r*, just as *hloili* also occurs as *loili*. Closer comparison, however, shows that *hrosch* arose from *horsch*, which has the same meaning, just as *hroyr* arose from *hoyrooy* and *heri*. The resemblance in sound to the Indian word is therefore merely accidental.

evidence.excerpt: The 1906 print reads *zu Adjectiven gewordene Substantiva*, ‘nouns that have become adjectives’. In §93 Humboldt describes the reverse process, forming nouns from adjectives, which also fits his account here of objects named for salient properties. The example of naming for a property occurs in §91. §93 refers in print to §90. The manuscript reading remains to be checked.

evidence.excerpt: German *Gans* and Sanskrit *haṃsá-* are cognates inherited through different branches of Indo-European. German inherited its form through Germanic. See Lloyd and Lühr’s [entry for *gans*](https://ewa.saw-leipzig.de/articles/50320/de).

evidence.excerpt: The German leaves the first element unexpressed in *eines ursprünglichen*. The English supplies *verb* from the preceding *Verba*. The parallel with the second element also supports ‘one original stem with another’.
evidence.statement: The alternatives change the description of lexical verb formation.

evidence.excerpt: The print has *ihn*, a masculine singular pronoun whose nearest grammatical antecedent is *Theil*, the material part of language. The English supplies *these changes* because the closing argument concerns what a full study of language must also include.
evidence.statement: The printed construction leaves the scope of the conclusion open to textual clarification.

evidence.excerpt: A *presentation* is how an object becomes present to someone’s mind. The object can be corporeal or formed by the mind. A word gives the concept a shape from a particular standpoint, and the presentation given by the word continues to act alongside the individual’s presentation of the object. *Apprehension* names the way of taking up the object.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: The sound of a word can continue across generations while its content varies. The German terms for sound overlap. In §91 *Schall* draws attention to the audible sound that may stay the same even when the word as actually thought or spoken changes.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: In §90 a word’s *matter* is how it presents objects along the logical, sensory and affective lines set out in §87. Its *form* is how the faculties work together in those respects. In §89 sensory and affective content is transformed by imagination, which can preserve it as form. *Material* also names what the words provide for discourse in §72.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: The *motivating meaning* is what gives a word its particular way of designating a concept. It can lie in a perceptible feature of a thing or in a metaphor. Humboldt distinguishes cases where speakers still feel the motivation from those where a historical investigator can recover it.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: A sign in the strict sense designates something with an existence of its own. A concept takes its completed shape through a word. The natural form of a symbol can stand on its own, and its idea can be seen throughout that form. A word can have symbolic properties even though its sound and concept have the more tightly joined relation described in §101.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: Each language makes a view of the world available through its ways of forming and designating concepts. There is room within that view for individual modes of presentation and for changes in language and thought over time.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: A stem word is a starting point for an analysis of word formation. Root words can serve as stem words for derivation and composition and are constrained in connected discourse. The analysis traces relative starting points. Humboldt also rejects the forced assignment of every word to a proposed root.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: The term *feeling* includes the intellectual orientation that operates without clear reflective awareness in forming and using words. §105 distinguishes particular emotions from a combined intellectual and affective disposition. *Inner life* renders *Gemüth* where its affective capacities matter.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

evidence.excerpt: Humboldt lists *words of possession* among families formed by a recurring procedure. He explains the basis of the class through a factual relation of possession. The passage gives no forms from which to identify a particular grammatical category.
evidence.statement: Recurring local terminology guide, not a universal fixed equivalence.

text_version.body: Ein Wort ist ein Laut, der einen Begriff bezeichnet. Es liegt also in dem Wort allemal Einheit des Lauts, die bei verbundenen durch den Accent bewirkt wird, und Einheit des Begriffs. Das einfache Wort ist das wahre Individuum in der Sprache. Denn es enthält vollständig die ganze Verstandeshandlung der Sprache, es ist sogar selbst die Form, in welcher der Geist das in seine Subjectivitaet verwandelte Object wieder, als solches, aus sich hinausstellt (39.); dasjenige aber, was herauskommt, wenn man es selbst wieder zergliedert, die Sylbe und der Buchstabe, ist nicht mehr Sprache, sondern nur Element derselben. Alle, auch die zusammengesetzten Wörter sind die Bestandtheile, der Stoff der Rede, und in dem Wörtervorrath einer Sprache liegt also der gesammte Gedankenstoff einer Nation. Das Wort theilt die ganze, im Vorigen entwickelte Natur der Sprache, es hat dieselbe Objectivitaet und Subjectivitaet (40.), übt die gleiche Macht auf den Menschen aus (42.), und ist ebenso seiner Freiheit unterworfen (51.), es bildet die Gegenstände zu der eignen ideellen Welt, die in der Sprache überhaupt an die Stelle der wirklichen tritt (39.). Die eigenthümliche Auffassung der Dinge durch die Sprache liegt vorzüglich darin, dass die individuelle Subjectivitaet, sich immer gleich bleibend, alle Bestandtheile der Sprache auf dieselbe Weise nimmt und behandelt, an jeden sich anschliesst, und sie stammt mehr aus dem ideellen, als dem materiellen Theil der Sprachen, mehr aus der durch sie gegebenen Vorstellungsart, als aus den in ihr gebrauchten Lauten. Die Wörter, die in wenig veränderten Tönen, und bestimmte Gegenstände bezeichnend, von Geschlechten zu Geschlechten und Nationen zu Nationen übergehen, können daher nur wenig sichtlich diese Eigenthümlichkeit an sich tragen, die sich erst in ihrem Gebrauche, und in der Art, wie sie sich gegenseitig ergänzen, beschränken und bestimmen, offenbart. Wo also, wie bei den Sprachen ungebildeter Nationen, dieser Gebrauch nur aus dürftigen Sprachproben bekannt ist, da reicht die blosse, eben darum auch unvollständige Wörterkenntniss nicht hin die Eigenthümlichkeit der Sprache gerade von ihrer wichtigsten Seite zu ergründen.
